{{ElectionsKS}}
The '''2026 United States Senate election in Kansas''' will be held on November 4, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Kansas]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Roger Marshall]] is seeking a second term. He is being challenged by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] pastor [[Adam Hamilton (pastor)|Adam Hamilton]].

In the August 4 [[primary elections]], Marshall won the Republican nomination against minimal opposition. Hamilton won the Democratic nomination with 34.9% of the vote over a field of candidates that included former Kansas USDA Rural Development director Christy Davis and Army veteran Noah Taylor.

Democrats have not won a Senate election in Kansas since [[1932 United States Senate election in Kansas|1932]].

== Background ==
Though generally considered to be a [[red state]],<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newsweek.com/roger-marshall-speaks-out-against-ice-as-gop-fears-it-could-lose-kansas-12481531 |title=Roger Marshall Speaks Out Against ICE as GOP Fears It Could Lose Kansas |last=Rahman |first=Billal |work=[[Newsweek]] |date=September 24, 2026 |access-date=September 24, 2026}}</ref><ref name="NYT">{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/14/us/politics/jd-vance-kansas-senate-race.html |title=Vance Campaigns in Kansas as Democrats Target a Republican Stronghold |last=Bidgood |first=Jess |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=September 14, 2026 |access-date=September 24, 2026}}</ref> Kansas has shown greater competitiveness over time due to shifts in the traditionally [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]]-leaning [[Kansas City metropolitan area|Kansas City suburbs]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Glueck |first=Katie |date=October 5, 2026 |title=Pastor's Senate Primary Win Gives Democrats a Ray of Hope in Deep-Red Kansas |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/04/us/politics/hamilton-marshall-kansas-senate-election.html |access-date=October 9, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Republicans control both houses of the [[Kansas Legislature]];<ref>{{Cite web |title=What happened to GOP supermajorities? Kansas Republicans appear to win big |url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/11/06/kansas-republicans-appear-to-win-big-grow-legislative-supermajorities/76085263007/ |last=Alatidd |first=Jason |work=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]] |language=en-US |date=November 6, 2024 |access-date=September 24, 2026}}</ref> however, [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] control the [[Governor of Kansas|governorship of Kansas]], which they flipped from Republican control in [[2018 Kansas gubernatorial election|2018]], and held in [[2022 Kansas gubernatorial election|2022]].<ref name="NYT"/> Kansas has not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since [[1932 United States Senate election in Kansas|1932]].<ref name="NYT"/> Incumbent senator [[Roger Marshall]] was [[2020 United States Senate election in Kansas|elected in 2020]] with 53.2% of the vote, winning by 11.4% despite expectations of a close race.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas 2020 Senate election results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2020/results/state/kansas/senate |website=[[CNN]] |language=en |access-date=September 24, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Marshall keeps Kansas Senate seat in Republican hands |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2020/11/03/kansas-senate-election-results-2020-433577 |last=Bustillo |first=Ximena |website=[[Politico]] |date=November 3, 2020 |access-date=September 24, 2026}}</ref>

Graham, attorney ([[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]])<ref>{{cite web|title=Candidates for the 2026 General|url=https://sos.ks.gov/elections/elections_upcoming_candidate.aspx|publisher=Kansas Secretary of State|access-date=September 18, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260501151638/https://www.sos.ks.gov/elections/elections_upcoming_candidate.aspx|archive-date=May 1, 2026|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== General election ==
One issue raised during the campaign was Roger Marshall's history of suing over 700 of his patients for unpaid bills while he worked as an [[OB/GYN]] in Kansas. The ''New York Times'' reported that in at least 81 cases, patients were arrested at the request of Marshall's lawyers for failure to appear in court for their unpaid debts. There were 13 additional cases where an arrest warrant was requested, but the outcome is unknown. Most of the patients interviewed by the ''New York Times'' who were sued by Marshall said they lived paycheck-to-paycheck and did not have the money to pay the bills.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kliff |first=Sarah |date=2026-09-08 |title=A Doctor Sued 700 Patients for Debts; 81 Were Arrested. Now He's a Senator. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/08/us/politics/roger-marshall-obgyn-doctor-debts.html |access-date=2026-09-29 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Hamilton produced an advertisement featuring a woman who said she was arrested for missing a $50 payment to Marshall. The Marshall campaign sent a letter alleging the ad was "defamatory" because the woman was arrested for failing to appear in court over larger debts to him, rather than for missing one bill, and that she was subject to several other court proceedings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaminski |first=Anna |date=2026-09-28 |title=Roger Marshall alleges defamation in new ad about former Kansas patient arrested while in debt • Kansas Reflector |url=https://kansasreflector.com/2026/09/28/roger-marshall-alleges-defamation-in-new-ad-about-former-kansas-patient-arrested-while-in-debt/ |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=Kansas Reflector |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hudnall |first=David |date=September 29, 2026 |title=With new defamation threat, Roger Marshall is making a bad story worse |url=https://www.kansascity.com/opinion/article317419376.html |work=Kansas City Star}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Alatidd |first=Jason |title=What to know about Roger Marshall patient featured in Adam Hamilton ad |url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/news/politics/elections/congressional/2026/09/29/roger-marshall-disputes-adam-hamilton-political-ad-featuring-patient/91986984007/ |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=The Topeka Capital-Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>
